text:
The evidence can't tell us whether agricultural clearing caused the loss.

**What it shows:** Hansen/UMD mapped about 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025 (3.91% of the 345.6 ha asset). Nearly all of it (98%) was forest in 2020 according to JRC. The MGAP 2021 map classes about 13.1 ha as native forest, with none planted.

**What it doesn't show:** The tool explicitly says it does not establish the cause (harvest, fire, storm or clearing), nor whether deforestation or land-use change occurred. It also says nothing on legality or who was responsible. The native forest label is only territorial context, never a cause.

**Status:** The finding is pending corroboration. 2025 is the latest year in the series, and no later year has been observed to confirm the change persists.

**Next steps:** To test the agricultural-clearing hypothesis, you would need 2026 data to check persistence, plus evidence of what replaced the forest, such as high-resolution imagery or land-use data.
